# PayPerScreen

> Pay-per-call sanctions, crypto-wallet, website, email, and IP risk
> screening API, priced in USDC and paid over [x402](https://x402.org) — no
> account, no API key, no subscription. Every request is authenticated by a
> signed on-chain payment at the moment it's made, on Base mainnet. Built
> around the assumption that most real callers are agents, not humans
> clicking a button.

PayPerScreen checks names against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals
(SDN) list (fuzzy match) and crypto wallet addresses against OFAC's
sanctioned digital-currency address list (exact match). It also runs
deterministic trust/risk composites — no LLM calls anywhere in the scoring
path — against websites, email addresses, and IP addresses, each returning
a riskLevel (low/medium/high) and a redFlag when a severe signal fires. It
returns results and signals — it does not make compliance decisions for
you.

Three tiers sit on top of that data, additive, not exclusive: (1) raw
data — every endpoint below, as-is; (2) do-it-yourself case management —
sign in at /login and any flagged check lands in your own queue to clear
or escalate; (3) AI agent opinion — a `.../opinion` endpoint per check that
re-runs it and adds an LLM-generated clear/review/escalate recommendation
with reasoning, narrating the deterministic signals rather than replacing
them.

## Docs

- [Methodology](https://payperscreen.com/methodology): a complete,
  signal-by-signal list of what every check actually does, and what it
  doesn't check yet — read this to judge whether a check is sufficient
  for your use case.
- [API reference](https://payperscreen.com/docs): endpoints, pricing, the
  x402 payment handshake, request/response shapes, and honest current
  coverage.
- [Lists we check](https://payperscreen.com/lists): live record counts and
  last-refreshed dates for every list currently loaded — not a marketing
  description, the actual database state.
- [Reference client](https://payperscreen.com/examples/agent-client.mjs): a
  standalone Node.js script an agent can run directly — reads a private key
  from the environment, pays per call, no other setup.
- [Agent card](https://payperscreen.com/.well-known/agent-card.json):
  machine-readable service descriptor (skills, pricing, payment scheme).

## How payment works

No API key, no signup. A request with no payment gets back `402 Payment
Required` naming the exact price, network (`eip155:8453`, Base mainnet),
and asset (USDC). The caller signs a gasless EIP-3009
`transferWithAuthorization` and retries with it attached; x402-aware HTTP
clients (e.g. `@x402/fetch`) do this automatically. No ETH is needed to
call the API — only to send a query, not to pay for gas.

## Endpoints (see /docs for full detail)

- `GET /screen` — $0.02 — fuzzy name match against OFAC SDN
- `GET /context` — $0.05 — field-by-field comparison for a prior hit
- `GET /screen-address` — $0.02 — exact match against OFAC's sanctioned
  crypto-address list
- `GET /screen-website` — $0.02 — domain age, SSL cert, certificate
  history, SPF, redirects, security headers, web-archive history
- `GET /screen-email` — $0.02 — mail-server validity, disposable-domain
  check, domain age, mailbox verification, blocklist status, typo-squat
- `GET /screen-ip` — $0.01 (beta) — Spamhaus ZEN blocklist and Tor
  exit-node check, IPv4 only
- `GET /screen/opinion`, `/screen-address/opinion`, `/screen-website/opinion`,
  `/screen-email/opinion`, `/screen-ip/opinion` — tier 3, base price + $0.05
  ($0.06 total for IP) — same params as the matching endpoint above, adds
  an `opinion` object with an AI-generated clear/review/escalate call

## Optional

- [payperscreen.com](https://payperscreen.com): the web UI for humans —
  same API underneath, same live payments.
